newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports - Nov 19.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricketer Michael Slater has been dropped from the Test side, making way for Matthew Elliott to join the team for its first Test match against the West Indies. Despite an average of almost 48, Slater will miss his first Test since his debut seres in England during 1993. Slater has refused to comment. Page 18.

Australian tennis doubles champions Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge won the ATP World Doubles Championship final in Connecticut yesterday - their 12th win this year. The pair will now part from each other for a brief period to give each other space befre challenging the record for the all-time doubles winners, which stands now at 58, only 17 more than the Woodies. Page 17.

Despite rumours there is friction between New South Wales skipper Greg Matthews and other senior players in the team, the cricketer has confirmed the rumour as untrue and says he believes he has their full confidence. Matthews' captaincy has reportedly come under some scrutiny recently. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian amateur cricketers proved triumphant at the men's world amateur team championship golf tournament on Sunday. David Gleeson, Jamie Crow, Brett Partridge and Jarrod Moseley scored a three over 219 on the final day, for a 26-under-par total of 838 It was Australia's third Eisenhower Cup victory. Page 45.

While being anxious to retain US import Isaac Burton, NBL team Sydney Kings are holding off signing the forward to a new contract until he recovers from a dislocated elbow. The club said that while Burton's injury was "pretty much OK", they still wanted a specialist to examine the injury before he flies home to Los Angeles later in the week. Page 44.

British soccer coach Terry Venables appears to be the clear frontrunner in a remodelled coaching structure which may see him take control of the Socceroos without having to move to Australia. If Soccer Australia does permit Venables to coach from home, hew on't have to travel too far to see possible players for the English competition. Page 44.
THE AGE

American golfer Tiger Woods arrived in Sydney yesterday to compete in The Australian Open on Thursday at the Australian Golf Club - his first professional tournament outside America. Woods played only five holes yesterday at the green before rain forced an early departure. Page C8.

Tasmania defeated Western Australia by 141 runs in the Sheffield Shield match yesterday. Despite a brave innings by WA opener Michael Hussey, the Tasmanians, led by cricketing great David Boon, proved too strong at the WACA Ground. Page C6.

Australian jockey Jim Cassidy is preparing for his comeback to racing on January 1 after sitting on the sidelines for 18 months for his alleged part in the jockey tapes scandal. Cassidy was disqualified for three years for his role in the scandal, but recntly had the penalty varied so he could resume riding trackwork. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

The unofficial word following the announcement Australian cricketer Michael Slater had been dropped from the Test side was that he will not play international cricket again until he 'gets his head together'. Following the most sorrowful year of his career, selectors say Slater has been given the chance to let a worrying form slide bottom out. Page 80.

The fifth Pacific School Games will be held in Perth next month. The event, to be held from December 5-14, will see the best abled and disabled student athletes aged 11 to 19 travel from across the country to compete. Page 73.

Despite a best performance from Australian basketball centre Chris Anstey yesterday, South East Melbourne Magic lost its first game in its American tour. In the fourth game of the tournament, Magic led Arizona University at half time, but lost 101-86. Page 72.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Collingwood Warriors coach Zoran Matic is angered by reports he was overlooked for the vacant national soccer coaching position because of his accent. The alleged report revealed one Soccer Australia commissioner objected to him because of the way he talked. Former England coach Terry Venables is the frontrunner for the position at this stage. Page 58.

Women's weightlifting may make its debut as an Olympic sport in the 2000 Games. With the official breakdown of the sports yet to be revealed, the International Olympic Committee supported the inclusion of women in the event. The IOC has also decided to include women's softball. Page 50.

Despite recording a financial loss for the 1996 season, Australian Rugby League chairman Ken Arthurson has revealed the organisation would go ahead with international matches next year. Arthurson said the main reason for the loss was the failure of Superlague-aligned Great Britain to proceed with its scheduled Ashes tour and the abandonment of the ARL's proposed New Zealand All Gold series. Page 51.
